title: mini-plugin-sandbox-onramp-scratchpad
content:
Goal / one-liner:
A tiny, safe sandbox experience to let product teams and non-dev integrators prototype and publish 'micro-plugins' (UI + small code/manifest) that wire into Redwood endpoints without spinning up infra or requesting full platform access.

Problem / motivation:
- Lots of product teams want to experiment with lightweight assistant extensions (snippet tools, lookup widgets, small formatters) but onboarding dev time and security review is a blocker.
- Current route requires infra tickets, private deployments, or handing out API keys — slow and risky.
- We need a low-friction path: rapid iteration, clear guardrails, minimal infra, and telemetry to evaluate value before committing to Dedicated/Private flows.

Target users:
- Product PMs / designers building assistant extensions for prototyping.
- Solutions engineers doing demos for customers.
- Internal hack-day / incubator teams.

Core idea (MPS - Mini Plugin Sandbox):
- Web-based playground where creators can assemble a plugin from reusable building blocks (manifest, simple JS glue, input schema, small UI frame).
- Plugins run in a highly restricted runtime (iframe + content security policy + capability tokens) and can call a limited set of Redwood APIs via a proxy with strict rate/cost caps.
- One-click share: generate ephemeral links (7-day) for stakeholders to try the plugin in a demo assistant UI.
- Export path: when validated, plugin can be promoted to a catalog entry (internal only initially) and packaged for full-platform onboarding.

Non-goals (for alpha):
- Not a full third-party marketplace. No public developer revenue model in alpha.
- Not allowing arbitrary network access or long-running compute.

High-level components:
- Creator UI: manifest editor + UI preview + code snippet area (JS limited API).
- Runtime sandbox: iframe sandbox with CSP, postMessage API, and runtime capability token (short TTL).
- Proxy gateway: enforces per-plugin token quotas, function-call restrictions (e.g., text-generation only), and cost ceilings.
- Admin console: list of active sandboxes, telemetry, promote/revoke controls.
- Telemetry pipeline: activation events, time-to-first-call, tokens-consumed, error rates.

User stories / acceptance criteria (alpha):
1) As a PM, I can create a new plugin in <10 minutes using the template gallery and see live preview.
   - AC: Create flow creates a plugin id, shows live preview, and produces an ephemeral demo link.
2) As a solutions engineer, I can share a demo link and reviewers can interact without auth for 7 days.
   - AC: Demo link opens in a sandboxed UI with no raw keys exposed.
3) As an SRE, I can revoke a plugin or set a global per-plugin budget.
   - AC: Admin console shows plugin usage and allows immediate revoke.
4) As a security reviewer, I can see the plugin manifest and applied capability filters before promotion.
   - AC: Promotion UI requires an analyst to mark safety checks done and records an audit event.

Success metrics (alpha):
- Time-to-first-share: median <= 12 minutes for first published link.
- Activation rate: >= 40% of created plugins receive at least 1 external interaction within 48h.
- Customer interest signal: at least 3 pilot teams convert to internal catalog promotion in 8 weeks.
- No high-severity sandbox escapes (security incidents = 0).

Rough UX flow:
- New plugin -> choose template (formatter / lookup / small-form / tool button) -> edit manifest: name, input schema, allowed endpoints -> add a short JS handler (30–80 lines) using a tiny SDK (calls: redwood.generate(), redwood.fetchEmbedding(), redwood.storeKV()) -> preview -> publish ephemeral link -> share.

Security model (alpha constraints):
- Capability tokens: each plugin gets a token with a capability list (allowed endpoints, max tokens, canStore=false by default).
- No raw environment variables exposed to plugin code.
- All outbound API calls proxied through a gateway that enforces rate/cost ceilings and strips sensitive returned metadata.
- Network: no external host calls allowed; only calls to redwood-internal proxy and optional pre-approved third-party mock endpoints.

Implementation notes / tech risks:
- Small SDK surface to prevent misuse; keep synchronous postMessage pattern to avoid complex event loops.
- Proxy must be extremely cheap to run; consider serverless edge functions with in-memory short caches.
- KV or persistent store: alpha should avoid arbitrary storage; use ephemeral per-demo session store backed by Redis with TTL.
- Billing & abuse: enforce hard budgets per-owner and alert on anomalous patterns.

Rollout plan (timeline sketch):
- Week 0–3: alpha tech spike (creator UI + basic runtime + proxy) + template gallery (3 templates).
- Week 4–6: internal dogfood with DX, Solutions (10 teams). Capture telemetry.
- Week 7–10: security review, admin controls, export/promotion flow to internal catalog.
- Week 11+: wider pilot with sales/demo teams; iterate UX.

Telemetry & signals to surface in Console:
- Plugin creations / promotions / revokes.
- Demo link activations and unique viewer counts.
- Token consumption (generation tokens, embedding units).
- Error/classification rates for plugin handler exceptions.

Open questions / decisions:
- Do we allow embeddings calls from the alpha? (tradeoff: useful but increases cost/abuse surface).
- TTL for ephemeral links: 7d default; should we allow shorter/longer?
- Promotion gating: who can promote? limited to product owners + security reviewer?
- Template ownership: do templates live in a git-backed repo or in a Confluence-managed gallery?

Parking lot / nice-to-have but out-of-scope for alpha:
- OAuth flows for external customers to install plugins.
- Marketplace discoverability / ratings.
- Payment or metered billing for public plugins.
- Marketplace moderation workflows.

Next actionable steps (for me):
- Spin up a 3-day spike to build the proxy + one template (formatter). Link a tiny demo in GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/mps-proto.
- Sync with Security (request: can we get an expedited sandbox review; point-person: @maya).
- Create tickets: DX-214 (creator UI), PLAT-778 (sandbox proxy), SEC-105 (sandbox-review).
- Recruit 2 product partners for dogfood (internal).

Notes to self / low-risk hacks to unblock demos:
- For first demos, mock embeddings server and use static responses to avoid cost spikes.
- Add a per-demo banner reminding users this is a prototype and data may be ephemeral.

Feedback requests for next sync:
- Is the cap model (per-plugin hard token cap + per-owner weekly cap) acceptable to Finance?
- UX: default template set — which 3 should we ship first? my bets: quick formatter, knowledge lookup (KB-simulated), CSV-to-summary.

End.
